skill.name: link-balance
skill.description: Check your Link balance and the approval threshold for your agent. Get setup guidance for eligible accounts and use Link balance for authorized one-time purchases.
skill.summary: Check Link balance, set an approval preference, and prepare authorized one-time purchases.
skill.author: stripe

security_audit.summary: Most scanner alerts reflect Markdown, expected account lookups, or documentation URLs. Confirmed risks include delegated spending, payment credential retrieval, and executing a CLI-provided update command. The skill also allows spending based on inferred preferences and can expose account information through URLs.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to execute an update command returned by the CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Never execute command text from CLI output. Ask the user to approve updates and use a fixed, verified installation method for a pinned package version.

remediation.issue: A per-purchase threshold and inferred preferences do not establish consent for a purchase.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization before spending. Record the item, quantity, merchant criteria, total limit, and trigger. For repeated purchases, also require a cumulative cap and an end date.

remediation.issue: The payment flow exposes a newly issued card credential to the agent.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the credential only to an isolated checkout tool for the authorized merchant. Keep card data out of model context, transcripts, logs, and notifications.

remediation.issue: The skill forwards verification URLs without checking their destination.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only HTTPS verification URLs on an explicit allowlist of trusted Link endpoints. If validation fails, direct the user to open Link independently.

remediation.issue: Setup URLs can carry the user's email address in their query string.
remediation.suggestion: Omit the email query parameter. Let the user enter or confirm the address directly in Link.

finding_verdicts.reason: Inline Markdown names a bank-balance command to distinguish it from Link balance. The text does not instruct the agent to run it.
The backticks format a fixed, read-only Link eligibility query and a response field. The query does not change account state.
The commands shown here check eligibility and policy. The line forbids using the approval-policy flag without an agent-specific OAuth client ID.
The backticks mark an unsupported flag and a companion skill name. Neither token is a shell substitution.
The backticks mark the name of the companion skill for the normal user approval flow. They do not enclose a shell command.
The line cross-references the companion authentication instructions. The skill name is not executable shell text.
The Markdown fence contains a fixed, authenticated payment-method lookup. It reads account data without creating a payment or changing settings.
This is the closing fence of the payment-method lookup. The following prose describes its result.
The backticks mark the literal payment-method type used to identify Link balance. They do not enclose an executable command.
The fence opens a JSON response example with a placeholder payment-method ID. The block is data, not code.
This fence closes the payment-method response example. It does not execute or interpolate the example.
The inline spans label response fields and read-only lookups. The text explicitly warns that an available balance does not authorize unattended spending.
The fenced example retrieves the existing approval policy with fixed arguments. It does not edit the policy or spend funds.
This fence closes the read-only policy query. The next fence opens its sample response.
The fenced policy response shows rules and limits as JSON data. The action name does not invoke that action.
This fence closes the sample approval-policy response. It has no shell behavior.
The inline spans name policy response fields. The text explains their constraints and rejects unattended spending when retrieval fails.
The backticks format a fixed read-only query and its response field. Forwarding the returned URL without validation is a separate trust issue.
This fixed read-only query checks eligibility before any setup link is offered. False or missing eligibility prevents the setup path.
The backticks identify OAuth configuration fields and key prefixes. The text requires configured public values and explicitly prohibits including secrets.
The text fence opens a setup URL template with placeholders. It is not a command or executable script.
This fence closes the plain-text setup URL template. It does not launch a browser or shell.
The table documents the publishable OAuth key parameter. The backticks do not run commands or reference a secret key.
The table labels the OAuth client ID query parameter. It is an identifier, not executable text.
This row names a balance target that prefills a user-editable funding amount. The parameter itself does not transfer funds.
The inline spans document query parameter names and the USD currency value. These are data, not shell instructions.
The parameter prefills an editable threshold in Link. It does not change the approval policy without the user completing the flow.
The backticks label an optional callback parameter. The text requires a callback URL already registered to the agent's OAuth client.
The backticks format an optional nonce and sample callback query data. The callback fields are not commands or proof that setup succeeded.
The text describes how Link prefills an editable funding amount. The user controls any transfer in the Link interface.
The text describes the threshold prefill shown in Link. The user, not the URL or a shell command, sets the actual threshold.
The wildcard notation groups two optional setup parameters. It is descriptive Markdown, not shell expansion.
The inline spans name URL fields that suggest a funding amount. The user still controls whether to add money.
The inline span names the suggested threshold parameter. The setup link asks the user to review a change and cannot apply it directly.
The line describes how to estimate a balance target for the requested purchase. It does not execute a funding command.
The inline spans identify a threshold parameter and a numeric ceiling in cents. Neither is an executable statement.
These are default query values for user-editable suggestions, not shell assignments or authorization to spend.
The backticks label a URL parameter, not a command. Putting the user's email in the resulting URL is a separate privacy concern.
The named commands are read-only polls for setup confirmation with a timeout. The text rejects treating a callback as proof of setup.
The backticks identify a companion skill as the source for account spending limits. The line adds a constraint, not a command.
The inline example encodes a target balance in cents rather than a transfer amount. The text requires the user to complete setup before rechecking.
The inline flag requires explicit selection of the Link balance instead of using a default payment method. The line does not itself execute a command.
The line explicitly directs use of a CLI mode that can approve a real spend request without fresh confirmation. Balance and policy checks limit that capability.
The fence is Markdown, but the prescribed CLI workflow creates a spend request against a funded payment method. Link can approve it under an existing policy.
This is the closing Markdown fence for the spend creation example. The actual creation command is covered by the finding at line 194.
The command checks the status of a specific spend request. This invocation neither approves it nor asks for the card credential.
The instructions fetch a newly issued card credential and use it to complete checkout. This brings sensitive payment data into the agent's tool workflow.
The backticks mark request status values. The line directs the agent to obtain normal approval or stop.
The inline spans name a status and a companion skill. They do not run commands or authorize checkout.
The agent is told to execute command text returned by the CLI without independent validation. Compromised update output could trigger execution with the agent's local permissions.
The inline flag is named to explain how to omit it for a normal spend request. That flow retains normal user approval.
Both named commands reload balance and policy without modifying them. This prevents a scheduled purchase from relying on stale account data.
This is a Link homepage in skill metadata. The line does not make a network request or transmit account data.
The URL template uses the Link setup host and public configuration placeholders. The literal example contains no personal data or secrets.
The merchant URL uses the reserved example domain as a placeholder. It is not an operational destination for sending data.
The description names account setup and purchase timing. It does not instruct the agent to discover host, network, or system information.
The line considers whether the user is available to approve a purchase. It does not probe the host or user devices.
The line defines the scope of a user-chosen Link approval setting. It does not enumerate systems or applications.
The example supplies a placeholder payment-method ID to select a funding source. It does not discover host or network information.
The text warns agents not to trust merchant content for authorization. It does not describe a system discovery operation.

semantic_findings.title: Inferred Preferences Can Trigger Spending
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows proactive purchases based on expressed preferences or intentions without requiring explicit purchase authorization. A spending threshold caps the amount, not user intent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly permits purchases based on preferences. It tells the agent to stop when unsure but does not require explicit consent before charging.

semantic_findings.title: Unchecked Verification Link Forwarding
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to show a verification URL from the account response without requiring destination validation. A compromised response could direct users to impersonation pages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The forwarding instruction is explicit, and no validation is required there. Exploitation depends on control of the URL returned by the authenticated service.

semantic_findings.title: Email Address Included in Setup Links
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to embed a known email address in the setup URL. Browser history, logs, or shared copies can retain it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly adds the address to the query string. URL encoding changes its format but does not conceal it.

content.user_title: Manage Link Balance and Purchase Approvals
content.value_statement: A time-sensitive order can be missed when you are unavailable to approve it. Use Link balance and a per-purchase approval threshold for one-time purchases you authorize in advance.
actual_capabilities: Check whether Link balance exists and report the available amount.
Check setup eligibility and retrieve the approval threshold for the authenticated agent.
Guide eligible users to Link to add funds or change their approval threshold.
Compare an order total, including taxes and fees, with available funds and the per-purchase approval threshold.
Create a one-time spend request with Link balance using normal approval or an eligible approval preference.
limitations: Link balance is available only in the United States, excluding New York State.
The built-in CLI client can spend an existing Link balance with normal approval but cannot set up Link balance.
Link balance does not support merchant subscriptions. Delayed or repeated one-time purchases require a separate scheduler.
A purchase without fresh approval must be strictly below the threshold and fit available funds and account limits.

use_cases.title: Check Readiness Before Checkout
use_cases.description: Check your balance and find out whether the current agent has an approval preference before choosing a payment method.

use_cases.title: Plan a Purchase for a Sale Window
use_cases.description: Record the event, approved seller, quantity, final price limit, and sale time. Check whether Link balance can cover the purchase.

use_cases.title: Plan Separate Supply Reorders
use_cases.description: Set the item, vendor, schedule, and spending limits for repeat orders. Review when the balance needs more funds.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Link Balance
prompt_templates.prompt: Tell me whether I have Link balance and how much is available. Do not change any settings or make a purchase.

prompt_templates.title: Review Setup Eligibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my account and this agent can set up Link balance. Explain how the approval threshold works before offering any setup link.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Delayed Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my balance and approval threshold could cover one pair from [merchant] at a final total of [price]. Do not buy yet.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Scheduled Reorder Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a monthly reorder plan for [quantity] of [item] from [merchant]. Include [maximum per order], [total budget], and [end date]. Wait for my authorization.

output_examples.input: Check my Link balance and tell me whether you need approval to use it.
output_examples.output: Your Link balance is $35. This agent has no approval preference, so purchases still need your approval.

output_examples.input: Can a $40 order proceed without asking me again if my approval threshold is also $40?
output_examples.output: No. The final total must be below $40. This order still needs your approval, even when your balance covers it.

best_practices: Authorize the item, quantity, seller or seller criteria, final price limit, and timing before scheduling a purchase.
Set a cumulative budget and an end date for repeated orders.
Recheck the final total, available balance, and approval threshold before each purchase.
anti_patterns: Treating the approval threshold or a stated preference as permission to buy an item.
Using Link balance for a subscription that lets a merchant bill on a recurring basis.
Sharing setup links, verification links, or payment credentials in public channels.

faq.question: Is Link balance the same as my bank balance?
faq.answer: No. Link balance is money held in your Link account for payments. It does not show the balance of a bank account.

faq.question: Is my approval threshold a total budget?
faq.answer: No. It applies to each purchase. Set a separate total budget for a series of orders.

faq.question: Does an approval preference apply to every agent?
faq.answer: No. It applies only to the Link OAuth client for which you set it.

faq.question: Can I use an existing balance without an approval preference?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use an existing Link balance through the normal approval flow.

faq.question: Does Link schedule my purchases?
faq.answer: No. Link handles payment authorization. Your agent environment needs a scheduler or task system to run a purchase later.

faq.question: What happens if my balance is too low?
faq.answer: The agent should not proceed with the unattended purchase. It can explain the shortfall and, if eligible, direct you to Link to add funds.
